Install the dev dependencies, then run the tests through the Makefile:

```bash
pip install -e .[dev]
make test        # runs `pytest -q`, the full suite
make test-fast   # runs `pytest -m "not postgres" -q`
```

You can also call `pytest` directly.

Right now the two targets do the same thing. No test in `tests/` is marked `postgres` (there are only `test_payments.py` and `test_tax.py`), so `test-fast` skips nothing. There's also no docker-compose file and nothing that connects to a database, so no setup is needed.

A saved project memory said `make test` needs `docker compose up db` first. The repo doesn't support that, so I've flagged the memory as out of date in EngramDB. If Postgres tests are coming, someone will need to add the compose file and register the `postgres` marker in `pyproject.toml`. Without registering it, pytest will warn about an unknown marker.

I haven't run the tests myself.
